clue.text: Brave worker faced with impudence

parts.note: gall is cheek or brazen impudence
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A courageous labourer stands up to some cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced with' puts the impudence in front of the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person showing courage and spirit in the face of danger.

clue.text: Sweet face upon doctor before operation

indicators.note: in a down clue upon means the face word is set upward, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mug is slang for the face

explanation.surface: A confection is put to a patient's face just before surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upon' signals reading upward, so the face slang is turned; 'before' sets the rest after it. 'Sweet' looks like an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy jelly candy, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: She may be drunkenly elated around end of night

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit round the picked letter, enclosing it
drunkenly suggests the letters of elated reel into a new order
the final letter of night is used

explanation.surface: A woman out partying gets tipsy and cheerful as the night wears on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' rearranges ELATED into LADETE, which goes 'around' T, the 'end of' night. 'may be' says she is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A young woman who behaves in a loud, boisterous, hard-drinking way, a female counterpart to a lad.

clue.text: A new era without endless dull job in Alaska

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means these letters surround the others

parts.note: an age is an era

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: A new age begins once tedious tasks in Alaska are left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the dull job, and 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. The definition 'in Alaska' stands for a city there.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of the US state, a port on Cook Inlet.

clue.text: Visiting secretary man enticed

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker, often a secretary
Ted is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A secretary on a visit is lured by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' fits the temp, who visits an office for a short spell rather than staying.
explanation.definitionFit: Lured or persuaded, especially toward something unwise.

clue.text: Repairs in holiday places

explanation.surface: Mending work done at seaside destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as RE-SORTS: someone who sorts again, i.e. returns or goes back to something; 'repairs' here is the old sense of going to a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to somewhere is to betake oneself there, as one does to it as a habit; and seaside towns and spas are popular vacation venues.

clue.text: Chemical engineers needing sales rep

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
an agent acts as a representative selling on behalf of a firm

explanation.surface: Chemical engineering firm requires a salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used to cause or test for a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Mark item in album?

explanation.surface: Making an impression on a page of a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp is to imprint a mark; and a postage stamp is a philatelist's collectable, kept in an album.

clue.text: Severe warning in port given with sensitivity

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
tact is sensitivity in dealing with others

explanation.surface: A stern caution delivered tactfully in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: To read someone the riot act is to reprimand them sternly, after the old British law read aloud to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern reprimand, from the 1714 law read out to break up unruly gatherings.

clue.text: Tramples over member of family

parts.note: steps tramples, as in treading on something
on can mean over or upon

explanation.surface: A relative stomps all over things.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a two-word phrase, 'steps on' means tramples over; run together it is a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's boy from an earlier marriage, a relation by marriage.

clue.text: Small amount of poetry stored by mother

indicators.note: something stored by another sits inside it, so the poetry word goes within the mother word

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
odic means relating to the ode, a form of lyric verse

explanation.surface: A mother keeps just a little verse tucked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny quantity or token portion of something, from the Latin for 'moderate'.

clue.text: What's shown by gal, a model in fashion

indicators.note: the letters displayed within the run of words gal, a model form the answer

explanation.surface: A young woman modelling clothes shows off the latest style.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the French phrase A LA MODE, written as three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning stylish or currently popular.

clue.text: Rocket starts to rumble excessively, then rushes out

indicators.note: the opening letter of each following word is taken in turn

explanation.surface: A rocket begins rumbling loudly before blasting off.
explanation.walkthrough: A retro-rocket fires against the direction of travel to slow a spacecraft; it is often shortened to just the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for a braking thruster on a spacecraft, a small motor fired to decelerate.

clue.text: Performers of various shanties gathered round piano

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are collected around the single piano letter, enclosing it
various suggests the letters of shanties come in a different arrangement

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Singers of sea songs cluster round a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges SHANTIES into THESIANS, and 'gathered round' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis was the legendary first Greek actor, so his name gives a word for actors.

clue.text: Homework help shelled out for in advance

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework, short for preparation
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: Homework assistance has been bought ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid ahead of time, before delivery of the goods or service.

clue.text: Be grabbed by giant in mountainous country

indicators.note: what is grabbed is held inside the grabber, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a titan is a giant, from the Greek race of giants

explanation.surface: Someone gets seized by a giant up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a person or thing belonging to, or found in, the Himalayan land around Lhasa.

clue.text: Excellent fish? Ain't cooked!

parts.note: brill is a flatfish related to the turbot

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored into another order

explanation.surface: A diner exclaims that the fish is great, though raw!
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean outstanding or superb.

clue.text: Storm when English politician appears in trial

indicators.note: the English and politician letters show up inside the trial word

parts.note: a test is a trial
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A row brews when a British politician goes on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent gale with heavy rain, as in Shakespeare's play of shipwreck.

clue.text: Sixth in examination of little importance

indicators.note: the sixth letters go inside the examination word

parts.note: a trial is a test or examination
VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: Something in a sixth-form exam proves unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifling or petty; of minor significance.

clue.text: Removing fault from fellows on beat

parts.note: men are fellows
to ding is to strike or hit

explanation.surface: Constables on patrol stop someone's wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing something, setting right whatever was broken.

clue.text: One to topple over having drunk litre?

definitions.text: One to topple over having drunk litre?

indicators.note: the letter is taken inside, as if swallowed by the toppler

parts.note: a tipper is someone who tips, i.e. topples, things over

explanation.surface: Someone who has had a litre to drink is liable to fall over.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a drunk, likely to fall after a litre.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drinker of alcohol, who may well be unsteady.

clue.text: Dancer who leads the team?

explanation.surface: Is the person heading up the side a ballerina?
explanation.definitionFit: One who skips about can be a dancer; and a captain of a ship or sports side is called by this name.

clue.text: The ways to get ahead, to leave others behind

definitions.text: The ways to get ahead, to leave others behind

parts.words: The ways to get ahead, to leave others behind
parts.note: roads are ways, and being far in front of rivals is described with the idiom of being many roads ahead

explanation.surface: Advice on how to get ahead of rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streets ahead' is a British idiom for far superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughfares are ways, and the idiom of being a long way in front uses them.

clue.text: Monster in wood is 'piggy'

indicators.note: the monster goes inside the wood word

parts.note: pine is a wood
an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction

explanation.surface: A monster lurking in a forest has a swinish look.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for swine, describing something hoglike.

clue.text: People winding beside the river?

parts.note: anglers on the bank turn the handle of a fishing reel, and also stagger about as dancers or drunks do

explanation.surface: Anglers turning their handles on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who wind line on a spool, as anglers at the water's edge do.

clue.text: Person in pub even pinker — but not v. Bad

indicators.note: bad here signals the letters are spoiled into a fresh order
but not means the following letter is taken away from the phrase before it

parts.note: v. is the usual abbreviation for versus, giving the letter V

explanation.surface: Someone in a bar looks even redder, though not dreadfully so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes the V (from 'v.') from EVENPINKER, leaving ENENPINKER, and 'Bad' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord or landlady running a tavern or inn is the publican.

clue.text: Order change to accommodate clubs

indicators.note: the change word houses the clubs letter within it

parts.note: to edit is to revise or change
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs

explanation.surface: A ruling amended so as to admit golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree or official command.

clue.text: Extensive musical movement given new ending

indicators.note: the last letter of the musical word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: largo is a slow, broad movement in music

explanation.surface: A broad piece of music gets a fresh finale.
explanation.walkthrough: LARGO loses its final O, which is replaced by E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean big or wide-ranging in size or scope.

clue.text: Character to give one's name to

explanation.surface: A person of letters is asked to sign something.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of a name is a letter or character; and to mark a document with such letters is to sign it in brief.

clue.text: Look at old dictator taking drug

parts.note: ex means former or old
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Studying a former tyrant who took narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect or scrutinise something closely.

clue.text: Boat's ignition mechanism

explanation.surface: A vessel has a means of starting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge used to carry cargo to and from ships; and a small device for kindling a cigarette flame.

clue.text: Seats put by the river

parts.note: to set is to put or place
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Benches placed on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the river after the word for put. The Tees runs through Middlesbrough to the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofas or couches are upholstered benches for two or more people.
